name: John Charles Tashner Jr.

roles.title: Enlisted sailor, United States Navy, Oahu
In charge of a maintenance crew detachment, Betio, Tarawa Atoll
Chief radioman, electronics division, fleet plane pool at Majuro

summary: An enlisted sailor, twenty years old, at Pearl Harbor on the morning of 7 December 1941, and the first participant voice this project holds for that day. Born in Jersey City on 18 December 1920 and raised in Lynchburg, Virginia, by a mother who had left his father when he was three; he enlisted in the Navy out of high school at seventeen, and the family's own account of when contains a tension it does not resolve — enlistment on leaving school points at about 1938, retirement in 1958 after twenty-one years points at about 1937. Both his sons place him ashore in a barracks that Sunday morning, shaving, mustered out and handed a rifle; both say he spent the following days recovering bodies from the harbour. What came after is better evidenced than what he did that morning: duty entries transcribed from his service papers put him on Betio in Tarawa Atoll from October 1943 servicing PBY flying boats and Army B-24s, and at Majuro from May 1944 as a chief radioman running the electronics division of the fleet plane pool — aviation ground support and electronics, not deck service, which is how his eldest son describes the whole of his career. He married in 1943, refused a commission during the war for reasons his two sons remember differently, and retired in 1958 as a chief petty officer with four children to raise. The family names USS Selfridge (DD-357), a Porter-class destroyer commissioned in 1936 that was moored in Pearl Harbor that morning, and places him on the maiden voyage of the carrier USS Oriskany (CV-34), commissioned in September 1950; this project has verified that both ships existed and where they were, and not that he was aboard either.
